featured_reviews.name: Abraham Dhangar
featured_reviews.review_text:
My mother was admitted to Godrej Hospital multiple times due to diabetes issues, and this time she was admitted because of swelling in her right foot caused by an injury. The surgeon recommended hospitalization for an operation.

Unfortunately, the Dr. Kunal Veling, did not provide clear explanations and was quite harsh when we asked questions, seemingly expecting patients to understand complex medical terminology without guidance.

Post-operation, the recovery seemed to be going well. However, the next day, when he checked the wound, he treated it very roughly by unbinding and pressing the wound unnecessarily, and shouting at my mother to keep quiet despite her pain. When I told the doctor to do it gently, he responded rudely and started arguing with me.

Overall, my experience with Dr. Kunal Veling was very disappointing. I did not expect such unprofessional behavior from a doctor at Godrej Hospital. He does not explain the cause of injuries properly and communicates in a rude manner.

Moreover, he has the audacity to say do complaint to anyone I don't care, there are many people who do complaint about me and it does not effect me.

I have raised this issue with the hospital's Managing Director, hoping for appropriate action to prevent other patients from experiencing similar treatment.

I sincerely hope for a positive response and resolution to this matter with utmost concern.

Attached is a photo of my mother's leg showing the bandage dressing, which was done inappropriately .

Thank You!

featured_reviews.name: Natasha Wadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would like to thank the Godrej Memorial Hospital for the outstanding care and support extended during my grandmother's treatment.
The professionalism, dedication, empathy and expertise of the entire team made us feel safe and valued during the challenging time.
A big thank you to the entire staff at GMH!

featured_reviews.name: Silent Explorer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent experience with the hospital was extremely disappointing. The overall system feels more like a money-making setup rather than a patient-care facility, with several unnecessary and irrelevant tests being recommended.

It is also concerning that the hospital does not have its own MRI machine and instead refers patients to an external centre in Ghatkopar (Nivaran). The coordination there was highly unprofessional, and an ICU patient was made to wait for more than two hours for the test, which is completely unacceptable and shows a lack of sensitivity toward critical patients.

Additionally, the reception staff needs significant improvement in terms of professionalism, communication, and patient handling.

The OPD experience was equally frustrating. Despite having prior appointments, patients are made to wait for more than two hours. This clearly reflects poor time management and a lack of respect for patients’ time and comfort.

Overall, the experience was far below expectations. We sincerely hope the management takes these concerns seriously and works toward improving patient care, infrastructure, and staff efficiency.

Humancare team took care of all the small details and transferred my father safely to USA for further treatment. My father has pulmonary illness, humancare team made sure he get continuous oxygen support through out the journey and on high altitude while making sure he is comfortable through out journey. featured_reviews.name: Anil Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
My overall experience with the medical team and flight crew was positive. Both doctors were professional and caring throughout the transfer. Dr. Baig was particularly dynamic, attentive, and reassuring, helping to instill confidence during a stressful situation. Dr. Yadav was also supportive, competent, and compassionate. The pilot and co-pilot performed their duties excellently, and we felt safe throughout the journey.
The most important outcome was that the patient was transported safely and received continuous medical attention during the flight. For this, the doctors and flight crew deserve sincere appreciation.
However, regarding the aircraft itself, I would hesitate to describe it as a fully equipped ICU air ambulance. The cabin appeared somewhat cluttered and unorganized, making movement and working conditions less comfortable than expected. There was no visible inbuilt oxygen system, and certain ICU-related facilities seemed to be unavailable, requiring the medical team to manually manage and change equipment during the journey.
In general, a true ICU air ambulance is expected to function as a flying intensive care unit, equipped with features such as an inbuilt oxygen system with adequate backup supply, ventilator support, multi-parameter monitoring, infusion pumps, suction equipment, organized storage, sufficient working space around the patient, and dedicated power backup for medical devices. While the medical team handled the situation efficiently and professionally, the aircraft infrastructure appeared to fall short of these expectations.
I would also like to comment on the cost. Considering the facilities and infrastructure available on board, the charge of approximately ₹18 lakhs appeared relatively high. I fully appreciate that air ambulance operations involve substantial expenses, including aircraft operation, medical personnel, logistics, and emergency readiness. Nevertheless, the level of onboard equipment and infrastructure did not seem entirely commensurate with the amount charged.
My intention is not to criticize the doctors or flight crew, who were excellent in every respect, but rather to provide honest and constructive feedback regarding the aircraft infrastructure and overall value for money. It may be worthwhile for the management to review the equipment standards, cabin organization, and pricing structure so that the service can better meet the expectations associated with a fully equipped ICU air ambulance.
Overall, I remain grateful to Dr. Baig, Dr. Yadav, and the flight crew for their professionalism, dedication, and care. The patient was transported safely, which remains the most important outcome, though there is certainly scope for improvement in the aircraft's medical infrastructure and organization.
